dossier.architecture: Pivoting telescopic arm with compact roller gripper and added cone-centering floor intake.

subsystems.intake: Low-pivot floor collector centers tipped cones with mecanum/omni rollers and presents them for handoff.
subsystems.transfer: Collector rotates the centered cone into a narrow gripper; handoff angle adjusted to match hardware revisions.
subsystems.scoring: Pivoting, extending arm with low transmission and an absolute encoder measuring actual arm angle beyond gearbox backlash.
subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve with runtime generated drive-to-point paths.
subsystems.endgame: Autonomous modes include station traversal, retrieval and balance.
subsystems.controls: Safe arm waypoints avoid grid collisions; dashboard exposes piece/level selection and adjustable scoring setpoints.

versions: First event lacked the cone floor intake.
Earlier concept included a spindexer, which influenced the narrow gripper geometry.
Team credits Team 95 for floor-intake inspiration.
dossier.analysis: Study the way an added acquisition capability fits a pre-existing arm. A centered handoff can preserve a small gripper rather than forcing the entire wrist to become full width.
limits: Intermediate prototype and competition dates are not fully resolved.

context_documents.title: 2023-1577 · A compliant collector must hand off at the actual revised arm geometry
context_documents.body:
# 2023-1577: A compliant collector must hand off at the actual revised arm geometry

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A low-pivot collector uses mecanum/omni contact to center a tipped cone, then rotates it toward a narrow gripper. The extending scoring arm keeps its transmission low and measures actual arm angle beyond gearbox backlash. Shoulder-style bearing support helps retain bearings in flexible plates.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly credits Grasshoppers inspiration, seeks fast/light centering and explains the low collector pivot as letting impacts lift the mechanism rather than break it. Handoff angle changes must follow hardware revisions.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A wide pickup can improve acquisition while increasing the range of states presented to a narrow receiver. Compliance helps survive contact but must not erase the repeatable pose needed for transfer. Measuring the joint after transmission backlash improves observability; it does not mechanically remove the backlash.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test handoff after collector impacts, compare actual and motor-side angle under reversals, and verify bearing retention after repeated plate flex.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: 1577 Steampunk | Behind the Bumpers technical Q&A
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the team-authored posts and technical replies at these locators.
source_reviews.facts: Team credits 95, 6328 and 2230. Opposed bearing shoulders retain flexible intake plates with roughly 1.35 mm reported axial room. Team describes Motion Magic with gravity feedforward and at most two safe waypoints. Spring assists vertical retraction and opposes horizontal extension.
source_reviews.limitations: Ratio recalled tentatively by team and omitted here. Control discussion is retrospective and event configuration is unresolved.

source_reviews.title: 1577 interview
source_reviews.review_basis: Inherited synopsis. No fresh full-caption or visual review.
source_reviews.facts: Older dossier describes tipped-cone centering, narrow gripper, low arm transmission and an absolute pivot encoder.
source_reviews.limitations: Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Jesko scores with a pivoting telescope and narrow roller gripper. The retained interview says a later floor cone collector was added to make more supply poses usable. It receives the cone and presents it to the existing small gripper. The team's written explanation adds two details that materially affect reuse. The collector bearings accommodate flexible plates, and arm coordination routes through a small number of safe intermediate poses while controlling the pivot and extension together.
piece_flow: The inherited account says the floor collector gathers and centers a tipped cone with angled rollers.
Rotate the centered cone into the narrow gripper. Pickup succeeds only if the cone reaches an orientation the gripper can retain after the collector withdraws.
Pivot and extend through permitted waypoints, place at the node and recover. Direct gripper routes and handoff routes share the scoring arm.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The floor collector adds a volume between the bumper and the narrow gripper and gives the existing arm a new collection posture. Waypoints must keep both pieces and mechanisms clear during deployment and at intermediate joint positions. The retraction spring changes the telescope's force budget with pose. At near-vertical extension it helps draw a cone back. With the arm horizontal it consumes some outward drive effort.

subsystems.name: Compliant floor collector
subsystems.construction: Team describes opposed bearing shoulders around flexible plates with the inner ring free. The plate is retained between shoulders and the shaft is tapped for end screws.
subsystems.operation: Older synopsis reports centering and rotating a cone into the claw.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team sought a robust spinning axle while preserving polycarbonate flex and avoiding clamping holes in the plate.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Distinguish flex needed for capture from movement that lets the axle cock or bind. The reported clearance depends on this bearing and plate geometry.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector shaft, compliant plate and cone orientation determine the handoff position.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check edge wear, screw retention and axial movement with a cone jammed on one side. Test debris tolerance.
subsystems.unknowns: Full roller layout, plate deflection under load and final handoff dimensions.

subsystems.name: Telescope and spring
subsystems.construction: Team describes a retraction-assisting spring and fast extension gearing. Older account describes low transmission placement.
subsystems.operation: Run shoulder pivot and extension together when clear. The spring aids loaded retraction and resists extension.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team says fast gearing made pulling a cone with the arm vertical difficult enough for the spring to help.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Size drive force against horizontal extension, vertical loaded retraction and full extension. An assist in one direction can consume actuator margin in another.
subsystems.interfaces: Spring preload and arm pose change motor load. Loaded extension changes chassis stability and joint torque.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare stall margin and heat through repeated cycles, then check recovery at reduced battery voltage.
subsystems.unknowns: Spring force curve, verified ratio and duty-cycle logs.

subsystems.name: Waypoint controls
subsystems.construction: Team reports Motion Magic, gravity feedforward and a planner adding up to two safe intermediate waypoints.
subsystems.operation: Select a feasible transition around chassis and grid obstacles before final joint commands.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team describes this as a simpler planner than generating a full joint trajectory.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Endpoint validity alone is insufficient. Joint axes reaching setpoints at different speeds can sweep outside the intended route.
subsystems.interfaces: Clearance depends on chassis approach, loaded piece envelope and relative actuator timing.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test interrupted moves, position error and constrained travel after a missed handoff.
subsystems.unknowns: Interlock logic, thresholds and measured margins.

revisions: Older account places floor collector after first event and links narrow tool to earlier spindexer exploration. Team independently confirms multiple collector influences and later explains spring/control design.
transferable_principles: When adding a floor collector to a compact scoring tool, use the collector to resolve piece orientation and explicitly map the resulting handoff envelope.
disconfirming_conditions: A centered handoff fails when supply orientation spread exceeds the passive capture geometry. A spring assist becomes counterproductive if added extension load sets the cycle time.
remaining_gaps: Full interview, installed dates, geometry, spring data and actual path thresholds.
recommended_images: Team post 4 bearing cross-section and a source-linked loaded handoff sequence.
